topic: Someone receives a package intended for the previous tenant
text: The rain was like an old friend, constant and weary, as I stood on the stoop, the package in my gloved hand. The address was right, but the name on the box wasn't. I leaned against the doorframe, the paper dampening in my grip. Whoever this was for, they weren't here anymore. The building was quiet, the kind of silence that carries too many echoes. I traced the letters of the old tenant's name, a name now belonging to a ghost of this place. I didn't linger, just left the package on the mat, where it could be found. Some things are better left undelivered, especially in a city where the past has a habit of catching up, no matter how many times you try to shake it.
